challenges.title: Shift Operations, 3-Week Averaging and Art. 100

items.title: Shift Operations Beyond 8h/48h (Art. 100)
items.text: With ministry approval, employers running shift operations (العمل بنظام المناوبات) may exceed 8 hours per day or 48 hours per week — provided the average over 3 weeks comes back to 8h/48h.

items.title: Up to 9h/Day for Intermittent Duties
items.text: For staff categories with intermittent (non-continuous) duties, Art. 100 allows up to 9 hours per day — nearly impossible to track by hand across many wards and rotations.

items.title: Overtime Still under Art. 107
items.text: Even in shift operations, every overtime hour must be paid at the hourly wage plus 50% of the base wage (effectively 150%).

solutions.title: How Klacks Takes the Load Off Hospitals in Saudi Arabia

items.title: Gap-Free 24/7 Coverage
items.text: Day, evening and night shifts across all wards — Klacks flags every gap instantly and fills it automatically on request.

items.title: 3-Week Average Calculated under Art. 100
items.text: Klacks monitors the rolling 3-week average live and warns before the average of 8h/48h is exceeded — on request, Klacks enforces the excess as a hard block, only overridable with documented supervisor approval.

items.title: 9-Hour Limit for Intermittent Duties
items.text: Categories with intermittent duties are correctly scheduled with up to 9 hours per day.

items.title: Overtime Premium Calculated Automatically
items.text: The statutory 50% premium on the base wage (Art. 107) is calculated automatically for every overtime hour.

items.title: Qualifications & Wards
items.text: Every shift is assigned only to appropriately qualified staff — per ward, department and role.

items.title: On-Premise: Data Stays In-House
